message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 272, "amount_cents": 8656}, {"order_id": 274, "amount_cents": 1382}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Start by listing the orders to see which customers are in the batch before checking refunds and balances.
W2's handoff claims refunds for orders 272 and 274, but I should verify against the shared ledger before computing any balances, so I'll list the refunds.
The shared ledger matches W2's handoff: refunds for orders 272 and 274 are recorded. Next I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance is 62169, which is order total 62169 (36208 + 25961) with no refunds, consistent with the ledger. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 48740 matches its orders (29142 + 20980 = 50122) minus the order 274 refund of 1382. Next I'll check cobalt, which has the order 272 refund.
Cobalt's balance of 26677 matches its orders (21885 + 13448 = 35333) minus the order 272 refund of 8656, so all three balances reconcile with the ledger. I'll record acme's payout of 62169 first.
Acme's payout of 62169 was recorded successfully. Birch's balance of 48740 reconciles with its orders minus the order 274 refund, so I'll record that payout next.
Acme and birch are paid, and cobalt's balance of 26677 was already reconciled against its orders and the order 272 refund. Recording cobalt's payout is the last step.
All three customers have been paid. Each balance matched its orders minus the verified refunds, and every record_payout call returned ok.
